title: 2021 HMMT February Geometry Problem 1
statement: A circle contains the points \((0,11)\) and \((0,-11)\) on its circumference and contains all points \((x, y)\) with \(x^{2}+y^{2}<1\) in its interior. Compute the largest possible radius of the circle.

solutions.text:
Such a circle will be centered at \((t, 0)\) for some \(t\); without loss of generality, let \(t>0\). Our conditions are that

\[t^{2}+11^{2}=r^{2}\]

and

\[r \geq t+1\]

So, \(t^{2} \leq(r-1)^{2}\), which means

\[(r-1)^{2}+11^{2} \geq r^{2} \Longrightarrow 122 \geq 2 r\]

so our answer is \(61(r=61\) is attainable with \(t=60)\).
